prompt:
Use case: isolated 4-second vertical dealership bumper for later editing in DaVinci Resolve or iMovie.
Primary request: A single continuous aerial establishing shot of a fictional small-town dealership called Buddy Garrity Downtown John Deere, Ford, Lincoln-Mercury in downtown New Hope, Pennsylvania. The property is compact and locally owned, surrounded by older brick storefronts, narrow streets, modest trees, utility poles, and historic small-town buildings. The dealership has a low, boxy, worn-but-maintained building and parking lot with a few green-and-yellow John Deere agricultural machines, ordinary pickup trucks and sedans, one large dark-green-and-yellow agricultural/security mech parked near the service bay, and a second similar mech visible in the lot. The mechs are treated as completely ordinary specialty equipment at this practical local dealership.
Scene/background: Downtown New Hope, Pennsylvania; older muted brick buildings, narrow streets, modest trees, utility poles, pale blue sky, gray pavement, compact dealership property.
Subject: Low boxy dealership building, service bay, dealership sign/main entrance, green-and-yellow farm machines, ordinary trucks and sedans, two heavy industrial agricultural mechs with dark green armored bodies, yellow construction panels, black hydraulic joints, exposed cables, chunky articulated legs, broad mechanical feet, and slightly oversized proportions.
Action: Over four seconds, begin with an awkward aerial view, drift slowly and slightly unstably across the property, hold the ordinary-looking mechs in view, introduce the dealership graphic late in the shot, then make a brief clumsy push-in toward the dealership sign or main entrance. Keep every motion slow and readable.
Camera: Vertical 9:16 aerial shot from an inexpensive early consumer drone or helicopter camera; gently drifting, mildly unstable, slow, imperfect exposure, soft focus, limited dynamic range, VHS-era interlacing-like texture and faint analog color bleed. No fast cuts; one continuous shot.
Lighting/mood: Flat daylight with washed-out highlights, earnest civic-minded local-TV-commercial mood, unintentionally funny because enormous mechanized farm/security equipment is presented with calm confidence.
Color palette: Slightly washed-out John Deere green and yellow, pale blue sky, gray pavement, muted brick red and brown, faded gold.
Style/format: Low-budget early-to-mid 1990s local cable-access dealership commercial transferred from VHS; mild video noise, soft focus, analog bleed, restrained contrast, no glossy brand-commercial polish. Clean frame edges and full vertical composition.
Timing/beats: 0.0-1.3 seconds awkward high aerial establish; 1.3-3.0 seconds slow drift across the lot with both mechs and ordinary vehicles visible; 2.2-4.0 seconds dealership graphic appears and remains stable and legible through the final second; 3.2-4.0 seconds brief clumsy push-in toward the sign or main entrance.
Audio: Silence only. No dialogue, narration, music, ambience, or sound effects.
Text (verbatim): "BUDDY GARRITY" on line one; "DOWNTOWN" on line two; "JOHN DEERE • FORD • LINCOLN-MERCURY" on line three. Use a basic dark-green rectangular lower-third or brief centered banner with yellow block lettering, a thin gold line, a simple abstract deer or mechanical farm-animal emblem, and dated in-house cable-company typography. Keep all text stable, centered, and legible for the final second.
Constraints: Fictional dealership; preserve the exact supplied dealership wording and punctuation; show the dealership and its green-and-yellow colors clearly; keep the two mechs grounded as heavy agricultural specialty equipment sold alongside ordinary vehicles; full vertical 9:16 frame; isolated insert with no preceding or following scene; no audio.
Avoid: People with visible faces, subtitles beyond the dealership graphic, fast cuts, explosions, combat, dystopian destruction, futuristic city, military convoy, sleek corporate dealership, glossy blockbuster lighting, cinematic lens flares, dramatic science-fiction atmosphere, photorealistic brand-commercial polish, excessive camera movement, unreadable or distorted signage, extra slogans, watermarks, and clipped frame edges.
